# Comparison with other libraries

<!-- Generated by benchmarks/compare.js. Don't edit by hand: rerun it with --markdown benchmarks/RESULTS.md. -->

Measured on 2026-11-19 with Node v26.13.1 on an Apple M4 Max. Each time is the median of 5 processes, each running the case for at least 300 ms after a 100 ms warm-up; memory is the median of 3 processes. Lower is better. The ratio in each cell is relative to source-map-js. [How it's measured](README.md#comparison).

| Library | Version | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| source-map-js | 1.2.4, chore/bench-runner @ adace91 | This repo. |
| source-map | 0.6.1 |  |
| source-map | 0.8.0 | Rust compiled to WebAssembly. The consumer is created asynchronously and must be destroyed, and both are part of the timed work. |
| @jridgewell/source-map | 0.3.11 | Wraps trace-mapping and gen-mapping in the source-map API. Its addMapping() skips mappings that add nothing (gen-mapping's maybeAddMapping), so it can write fewer segments than the other libraries. |
| @jridgewell/trace-mapping + gen-mapping | 0.3.31 + 0.3.13 | Used directly: TraceMap for consuming, GenMapping with addMapping() and toEncodedMap() for generating. |

## Cases

| Case | What it measures |
| --- | --- |
| `parse` | create a consumer from the JSON string and answer the first originalPositionFor() |
| `parse-both` | parse, then the first generatedPositionFor(), which builds the original-order index in libraries that build it lazily |
| `opf-random` | originalPositionFor() × 10000 random generated positions |
| `opf-ascending` | originalPositionFor() × 10000 generated positions in ascending order |
| `gpf-random` | generatedPositionFor() × 10000 random original positions |
| `agpf-random` | allGeneratedPositionsFor() × 1000 random original positions (with a column) |
| `each-generated` | eachMapping() in generated order |
| `add-mapping` | create a generator and addMapping() every segment, in generated order |
| `to-string` | serialize a generator holding every segment to a JSON string |
| `memory` | memory one consumer keeps once it has answered a query in each direction (JS heap, external and WebAssembly memory) |

## Differences in answers

Every case's answers are checked against source-map-js's. `*` marks a cell where a library gave other answers that are also right, `!` one where it gave different answers.

- preact.js.map parse-both: source-map 0.8.0 gives a different answer that is also right on 1 of 2 queries: another of the generated positions that map to the queried original position.
- preact.js.map gpf-random: source-map 0.8.0 gives a different answer that is also right on 278 of 10000 queries: another of the generated positions that map to the queried original position.
- preact.js.map add-mapping: @jridgewell/source-map 0.3.11 differs from source-map-js on 1 of 1 generated lines (its addMapping() skips mappings that add nothing).
- preact.js.map to-string: @jridgewell/source-map 0.3.11 differs from source-map-js on 1 of 1 generated lines (its addMapping() skips mappings that add nothing).
